key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map thermodynamic phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions and identify where stable regions exist.
engineering_relevance: The study provides design guidance for more stable perovskite solar absorbers, showing that high-iodide compositions are most favorable and that Sn-based alloys have much narrower stability windows than Pb-based ones.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data relax structures efficiently.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes are computed across compositions while capturing disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to compute phase-stability free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, revealing composition-dependent stability differences and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on layered ML models trained on DFT data, predictive reliability may be limited when extrapolating beyond the sampled compositions, phases, or structural motifs.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
